title: edge SDK timestamp normalizer and latency watermarking
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: Latency dashboards and p95/p99 calculations are noisy for edge requests because of clock skew between client environments, language runtimes, and intermediary proxies (edge LB / CDN) that rewrite timestamps. Root cause analysis shows ~12% of slow tail spikes are caused by skewed span timestamps rather than real server-side work.

This ticket proposes a cross-SDK lightweight "timestamp normalizer" hook and a small wire header (x-rd-latency-watermark) that lets Redwood servers reconcile client-observed event times with server ingress times to produce stable latency watermarks. The approach minimizes behavioral change for existing users, keeps sampling semantics intact, and provides a safe rollout path via opt-in header + server-side heuristics when header is missing.

Scope: implement hook in Node + Python SDKs (edge/HTTP SDKs first), add server-side ingestion normalization in the telemetry pipeline, update tracing middleware for managed proxies, add tests and dashboards, and run a gradual rollout for 4 weeks behind a feature flag.
acceptance_criteria: SDKs (Node, Python) expose a zero-config instrumentation hook that attaches monotonic-sequence + client-timestamp headers to outgoing requests when enabled
Telemetry ingestion applies deterministic timestamp reconciliation using watermark + ingress time when header present
Dashboards show reduction in spurious negative/zero-duration spans and a measurable drop (>=8%) in queue/latency tail variance for edge-backed routes
Feature default is off; rollout controlled by account feature flag and telemetry sampling rules
No more than 1% additional CPU overhead in SDK happy-path benchmarks
Backward compatibility: when header missing, server uses monotonic heuristics and does not alter existing span sampling decisions
